findings.current: *I could curse him out, but I’m not in a position to.*
findings.defect: The draft makes Taekyung the person who could condemn Jonghun, whereas the source says that someone else might be entitled to condemn him, but Taekyung is not.
findings.rationale: The omitted general subject in 욕을 할 수는 있겠지만 is contrasted with 적어도 나는 아니야, explicitly excluding Taekyung from those entitled to condemn Jonghun.
findings.replacement: *Someone might have the right to curse him out, but not me.*
findings.source: ‘욕을 할 수는 있겠지만 적어도 나는 아니야.’

findings.current: I hadn’t known about the latter. Processing the monster parts was the Star Guild’s responsibility, and no matter how cooperative the raid was, Won Myunghoon was the commander who made every decision.
findings.defect: The draft narrows 부산물 to monster parts even though this sentence explains why Taekyung did not know the Magic Gem yield, and it misconstrues 협동 레이드 as a raid with a variable degree of cooperation rather than the established joint-raid arrangement.
findings.rationale: 부산물 includes the recovered materials at issue, while 협동 레이드 names the type of raid; the point is that the joint operation did not change Won’s sole authority over such decisions.
findings.replacement: I hadn’t known about the latter. Handling the byproducts was the Star Guild’s responsibility, and even though this was a joint raid, Won Myunghoon was the commander who made every decision.
findings.source: 나는 후자에 관한 사실은 모르고 있었다. 부산물 처리는 스타 길드의 소관이고, 제아무리 협동 레이드라고 해도 모든 걸 결정하는 지휘관은 원명훈이다.

findings.current: I had given it an unforgettable nightmare, and it had given me one in return.
findings.defect: The draft turns the reciprocal indelible memories into identical nightmares. The source leaves the nature of each memory open: the Wyvern gave Taekyung a nightmare, while Taekyung left it with its wounded eye.
findings.rationale: 씻을 수 없는 기억 means a memory that cannot be erased, not necessarily a nightmare, and the paired fragments deliberately emphasize the reciprocal but different marks they left on each other.
findings.replacement: Me to it, and it to me. We had each left the other with an indelible memory.
findings.source: 나는 놈에게, 놈은 나에게. 서로가 서로에게 씻을 수 없는 기억을 안겨 주었으니까.

findings.current: Sometimes, it was better to encourage fear than courage.
findings.defect: “Encourage fear” is an unnatural collocation and weakens the contrast between deliberately stoking fear and inspiring courage.
findings.rationale: 부추기다 means to stoke or incite something, while the comparison with 용기 calls for the natural counterpart “inspiring courage.”
findings.replacement: Sometimes, stoking fear worked better than inspiring courage.
findings.source: 간혹 어떨 때는 용기보다 공포를 부추기는 것이 낫다.

findings.current: Jin Taekyung’s lowered eyes looked unfamiliar.
findings.defect: “Lowered eyes” introduces a physical downward movement absent from the source. 가라앉은 describes the settled, subdued quality of his gaze.
findings.rationale: The line concerns the unfamiliar composure or weight in Taekyung’s eyes, not the direction in which he is looking.
findings.replacement: There was something unfamiliar about Jin Taekyung’s steady gaze.

findings.current: The skin on which every hair had risen was the witness, and my pounding heart was both prosecutor and judge.
findings.defect: “The skin on which every hair had risen” is an awkward anatomical calque that disrupts the otherwise clear courtroom metaphor.
findings.rationale: The replacement naturally conveys 솜털까지 바짝 곤두선 while preserving the source’s witness, prosecutor, and judge metaphor.
findings.replacement: My skin, with every last hair standing on end, was the witness, and my pounding heart was both prosecutor and judge.
findings.source: 솜털까지 바짝 곤두선 피부가 증인이고 두방망이질 치는 심장이 검사인 동시에 판사다.

summary: The draft contains one subject-and-negation reversal, one distorted causal explanation, one altered reciprocal image, and several localized English issues.
